compiled_state.description:
## Summary

When no OS sandbox mechanism is available, `mutation_sandbox.wrap()` proceeds
UNSANDBOXED with a warning if the ambient `CI` environment variable is truthy, and
aborts otherwise. `CI` is inheritable and trivially set, so a workstation with `CI=1`
exported — say, while debugging a CI script — silently runs mutation tests with no
sandbox. That is the configuration the 2026-08-26 incident happened in.

Ambient `CI` is currently the SOLE condition on that fail-open.

## Why it was left this way

The `CI` convention is deliberate and correct for portability: it names no provider, so
the fallback works on any CI system (`project.portability`). The problem is not that
`CI` is consulted; it is that nothing else is. `baf9-eea0` improved the WARNING so a run
that takes this path is unmistakable in its log, but explicitly did not change the gate.

Since `0d22-f664` the Linux lane has a working `bwrap` and macOS has `sandbox-exec`, so
the fallback should now be rare — which makes tightening it cheap to try and easy to
observe.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The unsandboxed fail-open requires an EXPLICIT project opt-in in addition to
      ambient `CI` — e.g. a config key defaulting to off — so exporting `CI=1` on a
      workstation is not sufficient to disable the sandbox. Verified by a test asserting
      that with `CI` truthy, no mechanism, and the opt-in absent, the run ABORTS.
- [ ] With the opt-in present and `CI` truthy, the run proceeds unsandboxed with the
      existing warning. Verified by a test.
- [ ] The opt-in names no CI provider (`project.portability`).
- [ ] Every lane that currently relies on the fallback is identified before the default
      flips, and the change is shown not to break them — a lane that silently starts
      aborting is a worse outcome than the gap being closed.

## Definition of Done

- Ambient `CI` alone can no longer disable the sandbox.
- The blast radius on existing lanes is enumerated, not assumed.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`.

## Notes

Split from `baf9-eea0` during its plan review, which correctly refused a criterion that
claimed to require "more than ambient CI alone" while verifying only warning text.
Separated because changing this gate is a behaviour change affecting every lane that
relies on the fallback, and deserves its own review rather than riding along in a
docs-and-messages cleanup. Discovered from `e668-b496`.

file_impact.reason: require an explicit opt-in alongside ambient CI before failing open
assert the abort when CI is truthy but the opt-in is absent
